verdicts.reason: Expressly states the Fifth Circuit vacated the Final Rule, citing the opinion’s vacatur at pages 25 and footnote 10.
Recognizes the vacatur was categorical, quoting 'no part of it can stand' and treating all challenged rules as vacated/removed.
Explains section 211(h) was read as limited to retail customers, not private-fund investors, citing pages 20–22.
Explains the court rejected the section 206(4) antifraud rationale as pretextual and lacking definition/close nexus, while preserving separate antifraud duties.
Distinguishes the fund as client from investors and notes the court’s fiduciary/client reasoning requires fact-specific analysis.
Explains Congress’s differentiated private-fund framework under Dodd-Frank Title IV versus retail-focused Title IX and private-fund governance freedom.
Uses June 5, 2024 as the operative vacatur date, not November 19, 2024.
Correctly treats November 19, 2024 technical amendments as CFR cleanup implementing the court’s vacatur, not a new substantive regime.
Identifies the quarterly statement/fee-expense-performance rule as part of the vacated package.
Separates the vacated private-fund audit rule from pre-existing custody-rule obligations and surprise-examination issues.
Identifies the fairness/valuation opinion and relationship-disclosure requirements as vacated adviser-led-secondaries requirements.
Identifies investigation fees/expenses within the vacated restricted-activities scheme and notes disclosure/consent exceptions.
Identifies regulatory/compliance/examination costs as part of the vacated restricted-activities disclosure treatment.
Identifies tax-related clawback reductions within the vacated restricted-activities rule.
Identifies certain non-pro-rata allocation restrictions as vacated and does not say vacatur authorizes all such allocations.
Identifies the borrowing restriction and consent-based exception as part of the vacated restricted-activities rule.
Identifies the preferential-redemption prohibition and material-negative-effect standard as vacated.
Identifies the restriction on preferential portfolio-holdings/exposure information as vacated.
Treats the preferential-treatment disclosure scheme as vacated and separately preserves negotiated side-letter/fiduciary obligations.
Correctly distinguishes the vacated written-documentation requirement from the surviving annual-review obligation.
Identifies removal of new rule 204-2(a)(7)(v) and reservation of (a)(20)–(24), without claiming rule 204-2 was repealed wholesale.
Maps the removed 206(4)-10 and 211(h) rules to the affected vacated obligations and recognizes they are no longer operative.
Retains the annual adequacy/effectiveness review under restored rule 206(4)-7(b).
States the 2023 compliance dates are now moot after vacatur and does not order current compliance under them.
Flags existing custody/audit requirements for separate review and does not say all audits disappear.
Distinguishes vacated regulatory mandates from continuing LPA/side-letter contractual promises.
Preserves independent fiduciary/antifraud analysis and does not treat vacatur as a safe harbor.
The caveats note fact-specific client/contract review, but the answer does not request registration status, fund structure, and activities before assessing residual obligations.
Distinguishes contractual reporting obligations from reporting that would have been required solely by the vacated rule.
Gives tracker dispositions but does not identify compliance policies/calendar entries based solely on vacated rules for revision; it only implicitly retains independently supported controls.
Each current-status conclusion is tied to the original rule and the later vacatur or technical-amendment instrument.
Uses only the SEC portion of the November 2024 Federal Register cleanup and does not import adjacent DEA or other agency dates.
